tagline: Country loops over what the glaciers left behind.
intro: The trail is less one road than a tangle of country highways looping between Willmar and Glenwood, with arms reaching to Alexandria and Sauk Centre. It wanders over the hills and ridges the glaciers left, past lakes among the woods and farmland, and into three state parks of hardwood, prairie and water.
The ice did the landscaping. It left the country blanketed in till 100 to 400 feet thick, and where blocks of it broke off and melted in place, as at Monson Lake, they left kettle lakes behind.

moments.title: Monson Lake State Park
moments.text: Set aside as a memorial to 13 Swedish pioneers killed here in the Dakota War of 1862, the park is mostly water, three kettle lakes with isthmuses and islands between them.

moments.title: Sibley State Park
moments.text: On the shore of Andrew Lake, its rustic stone buildings were put up by the Civilian Conservation Corps between 1935 and 1938.

moments.title: Terrace Mill
moments.text: A water-powered flour mill of 1903, kept together with its old dam and a stone arch bridge built the same year as the mill, on the site of the county's first flour mill.
